## Short Exercises {.section-heading}

Each one asks you to make a quick call about something familiar, such as a
favorite artist or the age at which someone becomes old, and then shows what
went into that call.

```{=html}
<div class="project-grid project-grid--pairs container">

  <div class="project-card">
    <span class="project-card-tag">Exercise · Measurement</span>
    <p class="project-card-title">The Hip-Hop Periodic Table</p>
    <p class="project-card-desc">
      Score a favorite rapper on gut feeling, then compare that score with a table
      of 187 hip-hop acts rated on five parts of lyricism, and see how much
      depends on what you decided to measure.
    </p>
    <a href="../hiphop/hiphop_periodic_table.html" style="font-weight:600; color:#B23A28;">
      Explore the periodic table →
    </a>
    <p style="font-size:0.85rem; margin-top:0.5rem; color:#6A5F72;">
      Companion materials:
      <a href="../hiphop/hiphop_dashboard.html">analytics dashboard</a> ·
      <a href="../hiphop/data_dictionary.html">data dictionary</a>
    </p>
  </div>

  <div class="project-card">
    <span class="project-card-tag">Exercise · Measurement</span>
    <p class="project-card-title">The Barnum Test</p>
    <p class="project-card-desc">
      Answer a few questions, read the profile written about you, and rate how
      accurate it feels; the reveal explains why a description that fits everyone
      tells you very little about anyone.
    </p>
    <a href="../barnum/barnum_test.html" style="font-weight:600; color:#B23A28;">
      Take the Barnum Test →
    </a>
  </div>

  <div class="project-card">
    <span class="project-card-tag">Exercise · Definitions</span>
    <p class="project-card-title">How Old Is Old?</p>
    <p class="project-card-desc">
      Set a slider for the age at which someone becomes old, a senior, or too old
      to drive, then see how far your answers sit from everyone else's and from
      the ages the law actually uses.
    </p>
    <a href="../howold/how_old_is_old.html" style="font-weight:600; color:#B23A28;">
      Try How Old Is Old? →
    </a>
  </div>

  <div class="project-card">
    <span class="project-card-tag">Exercise · Prediction</span>
    <p class="project-card-title">Trust Your Gut?</p>
    <p class="project-card-desc">
      Read short case files, predict who comes back to court, and see your
      accuracy scored against a simple two-question checklist.
    </p>
    <a href="../gut/trust_your_gut.html" style="font-weight:600; color:#B23A28;">
      Trust your gut? →
    </a>
  </div>


</div>
```

## Planning Tools {.section-heading}

These are for when you have an evaluation or report of your own to plan, and
they sort through the options with you based on what you have and who you need
to reach.

```{=html}
<div class="project-grid project-grid--pairs container">

  <div class="project-card">
    <span class="project-card-tag">Planning Tool · Evaluation</span>
    <p class="project-card-title">Which Evaluation Should We Do?</p>
    <p class="project-card-desc">
      Say what you have and what you want to know, and every type of evaluation
      sorts into what fits, what does not, and what could fit with more time or
      data.
    </p>
    <a href="../evalpicker/eval_picker.html" style="font-weight:600; color:#B23A28;">
      Open the evaluation picker →
    </a>
  </div>

  <div class="project-card">
    <span class="project-card-tag">Planning Tool · Data Storytelling</span>
    <p class="project-card-title">The Data STORY Worksheet</p>
    <p class="project-card-desc">
      The five elements of a data story, strategy through yield, laid out as
      seventeen steps you can fill in, with a one-page plan to print or download
      at the end. It will not write the story for you, but it will show you which
      parts you have not thought through yet.
    </p>
    <a href="../datastory/story_worksheet.html" style="font-weight:600; color:#B23A28;">
      Open the worksheet →
    </a>
    <p style="font-size:0.85rem; margin-top:0.5rem; color:#6A5F72;">
      Companion tool:
      <a href="../formatpicker/format_picker.html">format picker</a>
      (which deliverable fits)
    </p>
  </div>

</div>
```

## The Usual Subjects {.section-heading}

**Measurement and metrics:** building performance measures that hold up, and
knowing when a composite score helps and when it misleads.

**Data visualization:** choosing the chart that matches your argument, and
showing uncertainty instead of false precision.
